tob-10826: Magician and skeptical investigator Henry Ridgely Evans surveys the great mediums and spirit phenomena of the nineteenth century. tob-13326: Edwin Arnold’s Light of Asia tells the life of the Buddha in the form of an English epic poem. Published in 1879, it introduced Buddhism to millions of Western readers.
tob-4026: Baruch Spinoza’s Ethics lays out his whole worldview in the stiff frame of geometry proofs — definitions, axioms, claims — arguing that God and nature are one and the same. tob-0144-61626: The closing volume of the Secret Doctrine carries on Blavatsky’s braiding of East and West into one hidden system — more veiled history, more unguessed science. It crowns the farthest-reaching wonder-lore work of the 1800s. Theosophists take the four books as one revealing.
tob-4126: Reynold Nicholson’s choice from Rumi’s Shams-book gives the wild glad songs to Shams of Tabriz. These are god-love verses at their most wine-drunk — wine, dance, and longing. The volume first bore Rumi’s shorter poems to English readers. Nicholson’s renderings sing with the first fire.
tob-4226: Waite’s Black Wonder book — 1898 — surveys the devil’s wonder-books, from Solomon’s Key to the True Grimoire. His scholar’s handling sunders story from scare-tales. The book stays the classic English study of the black wonder-books. Needful for wonder-lore students.
tob-10626: The Life of Adam and Eve tells the first parents’ story after Eden — their penitence, Seth’s quest for the oil of mercy, and Adam’s death. This beloved pseudepigraphon shaped medieval legend and art. The text remains the great apocryphal expansion of Genesis.

arxiv-2605-09126: DiLoCo trains models across scattered workers that drift out of sync — staleness is the enemy. arxiv-2605-09326: Magnetically arrested disks — MADs — are black holes choked by their own magnetic fields, cooled by radiation into filaments. Akshay Singh, Damien Bégué, and Asaf Pe'er characterize their scale height and filamentary structure. The 2026 paper is high-energy astrophysics on nature's most extreme engines.
arxiv-2605-09526: Klein surfaces generalize Riemann surfaces to allow non-orientability; their moduli space is a counting ground. N. K. Chidambaram, E. Garcia-Failde, A. Giacchetto, and K. Osuga refine lattice point counting on it. The 2026 paper is geometry meets number theory.
arxiv-2605-09626: Rectifiable curves — those with finite length — in the plane seem elementary, yet old questions linger stubbornly alongside new ones. Boris Shapiro and Guillaume Tahar survey the landscape, old and new. The 2026 paper is a geometric tour from classical results to current frontiers.
arxiv-2605-09726: Testing whether an interference model is correctly specified — via exposure mappings — turns out to be impossible in general. arxiv-2605-09826: Theory of mind — modeling what others believe and want — matters for embodied agents acting in the physical world. Gurusha Juneja, Dylan Lu, Saaket Agashe, and colleagues build EnactToM: an evolving benchmark for functional theory of mind. The 2026 paper tests whether agents can read minds.
arxiv-2605-10026: 3D object detection for autonomous driving must adapt across domains, data sources, and modalities — without labels. Xiaohu Lu, Hamed Khatounabadi, and Hayder Radha build MUSDA: multi-source, multi-modality, unsupervised domain adaptation. The 2026 paper is self-driving perception that travels.
plos-pone-0003426: Archaeologists pulled tuberculosis DNA from a 9,000-year-old settlement in this 2008 paper. From Neolithic human remains, the team detected and characterized Mycobacterium tuberculosis, the germ behind TB. The ancient molecular evidence pushes the disease's partnership with humans deep into prehistory, supporting the idea that the germ evolved alongside us for millennia.
plos-pone-0003526: Neuroscientists scanned self-recognition in autism in this 2008 fMRI study. People with autism often show heightened self-focus alongside reduced social engagement, so the team watched brain activity as participants recognized their own faces. The neural patterns reveal how the brain represents self versus other, and where that representation diverges in autism.
plos-pone-0003626: Theorists Álvarez-Buylla, Chaos, and Aldana let flowers grow by chance in this 2008 paper. Modeling the gene network behind floral development as an epigenetic landscape, they showed random noise can steer a flower's form, not just a fixed program. The stochastic view recasts development as a system that harnesses randomness.
plos-pone-0003726: In 2008, Tzur, Levy, and Meiri tracked tiny RNAs as stem cells chose a gut fate. As human embryonic stem cells differentiated toward endoderm, their microRNA patterns shifted in step. The expression map shows small RNAs helping steer one of the embryo's first big decisions.
plos-pone-0003826: Working in 2008, a team peered inside freezing insect larvae with MRI. They tracked how cold-adapted larvae handle ice formation in their tissues using magnetic resonance imaging and spectroscopy. The in vivo view shows the tricks insects use to survive deep cold.
plos-pone-0003926: In 2008, Zhou, Li, and Kamei traced a doubled gene in bony fish. The IGFBP-2 gene, which tunes insulin-like growth factor action, was duplicated in teleosts. plos-pone-0004026: In 2008, Quintana, Mimran, and Carmi turned a stress protein into a peace signal. HSP60, the heat-shock protein, was found targeted by anti-ergotypic regulatory T cells. The stressed T-cell marker became a handle for calming harmful autoimmunity. The work reframes a classic danger signal as a promising therapeutic lever.
plos-pone-0004126: In 2009, Field, Bachmanov, and Mennella ran animal taste tests on hydrolysates. Plant-eaters shunned protein hydrolysates, while eager omnivores ate them freely. Two-choice tests split the diners neatly by diet type. The clean split reveals taste wired to each feeding strategy.
plos-pone-0004226: In 2009, a team reversed diabetes with cord blood. Human cord blood stem cells trained peacekeeper T cells that reversed autoimmune type 1 diabetes. The trained Tregs calmed the islet attack. The cell therapy hints at a diabetes cure path ahead.
plos-pone-0004326: In 2009, a German team stressed mice gently for long weeks. Mild ongoing stress produced joylessness and odd calm in mice. Activity patterns shifted quite subtly too. The model mirrors human depression's slow burn. The odd calm complicates simple stress stories.
plos-pone-0358426: Acute myeloid leukemia drugs given by IV or injection tie patients to hospital chairs for hours. This paper weighs the economic and organizational impact of switching hypomethylating agents to a pill form. Beyond patient comfort, the analysis counts real savings for hospitals — freed-up chairs, staff time, and beds.
plos-pone-0358226: Bronze Age burial urns from Northern Italy are fragile, and handling them risks damage. Comparing what researchers could learn each way, it asks when the digital copy is good enough — and what only the physical object can teach.
plos-pone-0358326: Sewers don’t lie: viral RNA in wastewater tracks COVID waves before clinics do. plos-pone-0357826: Barnacles and slime foul every surface in the sea. This paper tested zinc oxide nanorod coatings on micropatterned polymers for antifouling properties. plos-pone-0357126: How we see our own smile shapes our confidence more than any dentist’s chart. This cross-sectional study examined dental aesthetic self-perception, smile satisfaction, and associated factors among adults. The findings tell dentists what patients actually care about — which often differs from the clinical ideal.
plos-pone-0357726: Medicine’s compassion carries a real human cost. The synthesis maps what caregiving takes from the caregivers themselves — and what might replenish them.
plos-pone-0355826: Which patents will attract licensees — and which will gather dust? This comparative study predicted patent license outcomes using deep survival analysis. The models help universities and companies value their intellectual property and decide where to invest commercialization effort.
plos-pone-0354026: Power grids depend on communication networks that attackers would love to cripple. This paper proposed a risk assessment method for power communication networks based on LTA-EN. The method helps operators find and fix vulnerabilities before blackouts — or worse — result.
plos-pone-0354126: Fertility appears to shift women’s desire for conspicuous luxury goods. This paper found that higher fertility increases that desire — a provocative evolutionary psychology result. The finding links reproductive biology to consumer behavior in ways marketers have long suspected but scientists rarely test.
plos-pone-0345426: FDG uptake in transplanted kidneys was hoped to reveal silent rejection — but hope isn’t evidence. The honest negative result redirects the field toward better markers.
plos-pone-0355726: A strong sense of coherence — life feeling comprehensible and manageable — may protect against decline. This Aizu cohort study linked it to loss of independence or death in older adults. The protective association suggests that meaning itself is medicine.
plos-pone-0356726: Depleting the NECTIN2 protein slows one of breast cancer’s most aggressive cell lines. The protein emerges as a concrete therapeutic target for triple-negative disease.
plos-pone-0357026: Nursing students must learn to manage falls before they face real patients. This paper developed an immersive fall management program for nursing students and tested its usability. The usability study ensures the virtual training actually prepares future nurses for the split-second decisions falls demand.
plos-pone-0354526: Technology-facilitated gender-based violence is surging across sub-Saharan Africa — yet evidence is fragmented. This scoping review mapped what’s known about digital abuse targeting women and girls in the region. The synthesis exposes both the scale of the crisis and the research gaps that must close to fight it.
plos-pone-0356426: The triglyceride-glucose index — a simple metabolic marker — may flag severe coronary disease. This paper associated the index with coronary artery disease severity. The accessible marker could help clinicians risk-stratify patients using routine blood work rather than expensive imaging.
plos-pone-0354826: Kindergartens that move — outdoor, mobile early education — are gaining ground. The Moving Kindergartens protocol outlines a 10-week feasibility study. The planned research tests whether taking the youngest learners outside, systematically, delivers the developmental benefits advocates promise.
plos-pone-0355226: Changing stride frequency alters runners’ physiology — differently for men and women. This paper measured psychophysiological responses to stride manipulation in both sexes. The findings give coaches sex-specific guidance on cadence — because one stride prescription doesn’t fit all.
plos-pone-0351926: Brazil’s stinkhorn fungi — phalloid marvels — hid two undescribed species. This integrative taxonomy revealed two new Itajahya species. The discovery reminds us that even conspicuous, smelly fungi await description in the world’s most biodiverse country.
plos-pone-0353126: Nonordinary experiences — mystical, anomalous, uncanny — get appraised in patterned ways. This paper investigated the content and prevalence of those appraisals. The findings map how humans make sense of the extraordinary — a psychology of wonder hiding in plain sight.
europmc-pmc2793426: Doctors can track spreading cancer by counting stray tumor cells in the blood. europmc-pmc2797026: Barley breeders need fast ways to read thousands of DNA markers at once. europmc-pmc2803126: Protein shapes solved by X-ray can hide flaws, so scientists need a way to check them. This 2010 paper brings MolProbity, a free tool that vets these shapes atom by atom. europmc-pmc2876926: Too few subjects doom a trial; too many waste effort. This 2010 paper explains sample size calculation, the math that sizes studies right. The authors walk through the logic plainly. Their guide helps researchers plan trials that can actually answer their questions.
europmc-pmc2879426: Cognitive experiments need standard pictures, and this 2010 paper delivers 480 of them. europmc-pmc2889826: A tapeworm's larval stage causes alveolar echinococcosis, a slow, deadly liver disease. This 2010 paper estimates its global burden in cases and lost healthy years. europmc-pmc2981526: Alzheimer's genes point to the immune system and cholesterol. This 2010 gene scan links immune genes and cholesterol handling to Alzheimer's risk. The authors widen the suspect list. Their work opened new paths for treatment. Drug hunters now eye immune-calming pills.

europmc-pmc3027626: Trace pollutants predict obesity and diabetes. This 2011 paper links tiny pesticide and PCB doses to weight gain and insulin trouble. The authors warn of hidden risks. europmc-pmc3062526: Cell swallowing got a precision survey. This 2011 paper films cells gulping cargo with split-second timing. The authors capture the gulp in fine detail. Their work lights up cell biology. Viruses hijack this very gulp. The movies revealed unexpected pauses.
europmc-pmc3077926: Choices blend habit and planning. This 2011 paper shows the brain mixes map-like planning with habit in decisions. The authors reveal the blend. Their work lights up decision science. Stress tips the balance toward habit. Addiction hijacks the habit side.
europmc-pmc3094326: Breast tumor types predict patient outcomes. This 2011 paper links gene-chip breast cancer types to how patients fare. The authors' findings guide treatment choice. Their work shaped cancer care. Basal-like tumors fared worst, they found. Oncologists now test every tumor's type.
europmc-pmc3098226: A germ blocks malaria inside mosquitoes. This 2011 paper shows Wolbachia germs stop the malaria parasite in mosquitoes. The authors reveal the blockade. Their work points to malaria control. Infected mosquitoes cannot spread the parasite. Field releases are now underway.
europmc-pmc6591126: Intensive farming simplifies the underground: heavily managed soils host less tangled microbial networks and fewer keystone species in crop roots. europmc-pmc6602426: CRISPR began as molecular scissors - now it is a whole toolbox. europmc-pmc6614426: Quantum computers promise to simulate molecules exactly - but today's variational algorithms lean on shaky approximations. europmc-pmc6680826: Nuclear magnetic resonance - NMR - reads the chemistry of blood, urine, and tissues without destroying them. europmc-pmc6735526: ALS - Lou Gehrig's disease - still hides its causes. This update surveys the epidemiology: who gets the disease, where, and which risk factors keep surfacing in the literature. The population-level clues narrow the hunt for mechanisms and, eventually, prevention.
gao-gaoreports-gao-08-26: This 2007 GAO report takes Social Security reform past the usual old-age talk to the benefits paid for injury and to dependents. gao-gaoreports-gao-07-1126: Were buses and trains truly open to riders with disabilities? openalex-w7204549026: Cycling does more than build legs; it rewires nerves, hormones, and immune defenses. openalex-w7204657526: Rural settlers in western Parana practice politics outside formal channels, and this article studies what that means for democracy. openalex-w7204124426: When antidepressants fail twice, depression is called treatment-resistant, and options narrow. pmc-13467926: This 2026 review covered fruit-specific promoters in plants — advances, regulatory mechanisms, and applications in plant biotechnology. The tissue-specific promoters were surveyed. The review is the biotech resource.
pmc-13424526: A 2026 MIMIC cohort study of monocyte-to-HDL-cholesterol ratio and 1-year mortality in critically ill coronary heart disease. The inflammatory-lipid ratio predicted death. The ratio is the prognostic marker.
pmc-13469826: This 2026 protocol described a pilot randomized trial of the Healthy Choices intervention addressing stigma, alcohol use, and self-management in Spanish-speaking young people with HIV (the title is truncated). The protocol is the plan. The trial will test the intervention.
arxiv-2606-16026: Pathology reports — written diagnoses from tissue samples — hold huge amounts of medical data locked in free text. This paper builds a complete, reproducible pipeline for sorting those reports into categories automatically: from cleaning the data to testing the model the same way it would face real use. The work comes from cancer-registry researchers and targets medical AI teams.
arxiv-2606-16226: Chem code on big iron has scads of dials, and hand-tuning them burns pricey hours. This paper calls the right run dials up front for side-by-side chem jobs, using ask-smart rounds and fake-data drills. It is for chem-code pros who want swift, thrifty runs.
arxiv-2606-16726: Biologists compare microbe counts between groups — say, sick vs healthy guts — but how many samples are enough? Too few and you miss real differences; too many wastes money. This paper gives sample-size math for differential abundance studies. It is for biostatisticians planning microbiome experiments.
arxiv-2606-16826: Robot manipulation needs 'atomic skills' — grasp, push, twist — that combine into bigger tasks. ATOM-Bench is a real-world benchmark testing those atomic skills and compositional generalization: can the robot combine skills in new ways? It is for robotics researchers.
